proposals.observation: In the last 48 hours, 5 sessions landed on the quiz intro screen. Zero pressed start. Every single visitor loaded the page and left without a single tap. The furthest_step_distribution shows all 5 stuck at intro_load. This is not a traffic problem. The intro screen is doing no work.
proposals.proposal: The intro screen is almost certainly carrying either a vague value statement ("find out your money personality") or a friction-heavy promise that makes the quiz feel like homework. The fix is one copy change to the opening headline and subhead — something that names the specific tension these visitors already feel rather than advertising the quiz format itself. Joel's ICP arrives already anxious; the copy needs to meet that anxiety with recognition, not with a feature list. Replace the current headline and subhead with text grounded in the specific experience of earning well but watching nothing accumulate — the thing only Joel can name from the £150k story.
proposals.current_text:
Discover your money personality
Find out how your relationship with money might be holding you back — and what to do about it.
proposals.new_text:
You earn well. So why does the number in your account never seem to reflect it?
This takes four minutes. At the end, you'll have a name for the pattern that keeps playing out — and a clearer picture of what to do next.

proposals.impact: lift Money Worship open rate from 37.5% toward Money Vigilance's 66.67%
proposals.observation: The Money Worship automation has an open rate of 37.5% against 19 sends — noticeably below Money Avoidance at 52.63% and well below Money Vigilance at 66.67%. The sequence name suggests the subject line is probably framing "money worship" as a concept to be explained, which reads like a lecture. People open emails that sound like someone already knows their secret, not emails that sound like a module title.
proposals.proposal: Rewrite the subject line of email 1 in the Money Worship sequence. The current subject is almost certainly a label ("Your money type: Money Worship") or a question that telegraphs its own answer. The replacement should name the lived behaviour — the specific thing a Money Worship person does at 11pm on a Sunday — rather than naming the psychological category. One subject line change, one file. The preview text (if present) should be updated to match so inbox rendering stays coherent.

proposals.impact: turn yesterday's publish into a quiz entry point before traffic cools
proposals.observation: Yesterday's blog post ("Why do I avoid setting money goals because I'm scared I'll fail them again?") was committed and presumably published, but there is no quiz call-to-action inside it. The content queue shows only 2 posts queued and 46 published, meaning organic traffic to this post will arrive with nowhere useful to go. The Money Avoidance automation has the second-highest send volume (19) and a 52.63% open rate, which means this post and that sequence are aligned — readers who find this post are exactly the people the Money Avoidance flow is built for. Connecting them costs one paragraph.
proposals.proposal: Add a single closing paragraph to yesterday's blog post that acknowledges the avoidance pattern the reader has just read about and offers the quiz as a way to get a more specific read on their own version of it. No generic "take the quiz" CTA. The paragraph should feel like the natural next sentence after the post ends — grounded in the same honest register as the post title, not bolted on as a promotion.
proposals.new_text: If any of this landed, it might be worth getting a clearer picture of where your version of this sits. The quiz takes about four minutes and names the specific pattern at play for you — not money avoidance as a general idea, but the particular way it shows up in someone who earns what you earn and still finds reasons to look away.
